newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid says KLSE driven by weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Rashid says KLSE driven by weak sentiment.

text.p: Weak investor sentiment will limit the Malaysian stock market's upside in the near term despite earnings growth remaining intact, leading stockbroker Abdul Rashid Hussain said on Tuesday.

Abdul Rashid, executive chairman of Rashid Hussain Securities, said regional markets including the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange have seen some downgrading by foreign funds due to worries of a Thailand-like asset bubble crash.

"The sentiment has obviously been affected. There has been no fundamental change from our forecast of the earnings growth," he told reporters after the annual and extraordinary meetings of DCB Holdings Bhd, of which he is a director.
"In the near term, nothing much is going to happen until sentiment is right," he said.
Rashid said worries over the property market in Malaysia and the Philippines, after property-glut problems in Thailand, have led to portfolio adjustments by overseas funds.
Thailand has been battling a financial crisis caused by oversupply in the property sector and the slowest economic growth in a decade.
He said current Malaysian market valuation is about 16.7 times prospective earnings, at the lower range of its historical trading band.
He said Malaysian economic fundamentals were also improving.
"Overall, the market would continue to benefit from economic indicators such as the trade deficit and inflation and interest rates, which are all under control," he said.
